This trial executed the shipped selection code instead of re-deriving it: f263262 changes exactly 8 dispatch cells (Q8_0 and Q4_K, rows<=5120, batches 3,4,5,6, all MMVQ->MMQ) and 0 cells at any batch >= 16, so no gate point can observe the change even if it ran GGUF. learning: f263262's safety case can be stated exactly on CPU: it is an 8-cell tightening confined to Q8_0/Q4_K rows<=5120 at batches 3..6, branch-rule-identical to its parent, zero at every batch >= 16. That makes it provably gate-neutral and gate-unreachable, so a BF16 score of ~1.0 would carry no information about it and must never be read as gating F3. The remaining question is live dispatch, and the tracer is now sufficient for a short probe: one forward pass records ~100+ calls, so a 64-call cadence leaves a durable trace after the first forward instead of depending on graceful shutdown. Two honest scope limits: the measured table's raw g2 evidence is not in this snapshot, and the MoE dispatch path (fused_moe_gguf) is untraced (irrelevant for the dense Spark2_5 model). No new BF16 engine lever is claimed: decode is roofline-closed on a4, the sync-mirror family is already in the pending t4 candidate, and the long-context window change remains a semantics change blocked on >512-token exact-token parity.
